42196477.text: How would you describe Plasmic to a developer who has never heard of it?

42196484.text: It's a tool for visually building components and full pages for any website/app codebase!

42196491.text: You can use it simply as a no-code full-page builder that plugs into your own codebase, or use it to design low-level, complex, stateful components like autocompletes and date/time pickers.

42196498.text: One use case we're especially interested in is freeing up developers from requests from marketing, design, content teams, etc. These collaborators can instead directly create the things they want to see without being blocked on developers. Developers can in turn work on higher leverage things than pixel-pushing.

42196505.text: Plasmic is starting out as a pretty technical tool since we've been focused on letting developers build low-level components, but we're actively making the tool accessible to anyone, so that it's as approachable as a Squarespace or Wix (but for your own codebase). We're really focused on making it scale well up and down this spectrum.

42196512.text: What you build in Plasmic can be consumed flexibly. You can generate actual React code into your codebase, or you can consume it like CMS content over an API - and more. At the end of the day, the central point of Plasmic is about integrating into your real-world arbitrary codebase.

42196545.text: It's a browser-based tool so it's easy to jump in and start creating things on any platform. What you're manipulating is the "real thing," the actual web platform (DOM/CSS/etc.) and not (say) vectors in WebGL or another medium, so what you see is truly what you ship.

42196552.text: The workflow is: you create your visual designs in Plasmic, and then either (a) use the Plasmic CLI tool to generate a library of presentational components into your own codebase (into your local git repo), or (b) consume the content you designed via an API, so that you can treat Plasmic more like a CMS (and not need to touch the codebase whenever content is updated).

42196559.text: For anything that has non-trivial interactivity, all the logic/behavior (state bindings, event handlers, etc.) are all done from your own code, the usual way. So Plasmic isn't trying to reinvent programming, make you code via a GUI, impose any particular routing/state management, etc.

42203099.text: Problem: Quickly build and run experiments during busy tax season to optimize for conversion

42203124.text: With faster and cheaper experimentation, Turbotax saw XXX greater lift in their conversions to paid products.

42203162.text: Compared to previous implementations, Plasmic content takes less than half the time to implement and deploy.

42203196.text: By enabling marketing and design teams to launch experiments, Intuit was able to deploy XXX as many experiments in the same period of time.

42203243.text: "Plasmic has been a huge boost in value for us. Developers can focus on code rather than content, while non-technical teams can design and build marketing content that seamlessly integrates into our existing stack. By enabling these teams to launch their own messaging experiments, Plasmic lets us ship over twice as fast and supercharges our growth engine."

42203326.text:
Each year, Intuit experiences a surge in traffic around tax filing season, providing a highly bursty window to conduct iterative customer experiments. The faster teams can design, implement, and deploy new content, messaging, and features, the faster the company can improve the experience for its users and achieve its business goals.

Specifically, our partners in Intuit's CMS team launch dozens of experiments each quarter on the marketing website to drive more conversions. This includes the conversion pages for Intuit's flagship TurboTax product, seen by millions every day. The team uses a homegrown CMS platform to deliver these experiments.

Prior to Plasmic, Intuit faced the following challenges:

  *  Only a fixed set of CMS layout templates and building blocks are supported. Experiments strive to think outside the box, often calling for very new and different user experiences.
  *  All the building blocks are implemented entirely in code by software engineers.
  *  The number of experimentation iterations per tax season was bottlenecked by engineering velocity, not traffic and user segmentation.

42203358.text: "90% of experiments are thrown away. So we asked ourselves, how do we enable as many teams to create experiments as quickly as possible? Plasmic is opening up a new scalable way to iterate much faster at Intuit."

42203422.text: To accelerate experimentation, the team is focusing on the following key areas:

42203437.text: Democratize implementation: Enable non-developers, such as designers and marketers, to implement new content and variations quickly.

42203465.text: Double the number of experiments conducted per season: Reduce the cost of implementation to drastically increase the number of experiments running in A/B tests.

42203494.text: Incremental adoption: Work within the existing tech stack and allow teammates to start with limited surfaces, without requiring a full re-implementation or port of existing work.

42203523.text: A scalable approach: Allow many teams to build experiments in parallel without conflicting with each other, scaling with business needs.

42203573.text: "We only have a window of 6-8 weeks leading up to a tax season peak to launch experiments, where we launch, get confidence in results, and roll it into the baseline. With everything from small tweaks to big swings, Plasmic helps us more than double what we can do within this short window."

42203639.text:
James Armenta, the lead engineer defining a new process of rapid experimentation and innovation, evaluated a number of options — from evolving their existing CMS platform, to other page-building solutions. He needed something that could easily plug into Intuit's existing tech stack, while enabling non-technical users to create rich visual content quickly.

With Plasmic, they found a solution that helps with:

42203663.text: WYSIWYG page and component builder: Plasmic Studio makes it easy for anyone to visually create new pages and content, shipping to production with high design fidelity and speed.

42203691.text: Accelerate A/B testing: Plasmic projects can be easily cloned, tweaked, and immediately deployed to a user segment with minimal developer involvement.

42203720.text: Seamless integration: Plasmic flexibly integrates into any codebase, making it easy to leverage existing pipelines and workflows. It even supports bringing your existing components into the drag-and-drop editor.

42203749.text: Team empowerment: Plasmic enables non-technical teams (e.g. in marketing and design) to implement and own their experiments, without requiring a developer in the critical path. This allowed them to quickly scale their experimentation efforts.

42203781.text: Plasmic makes it easy for anyone on the team to create and update rich experiences, giving non-technical teams the ability to ship high-impact pages, such as Intuit's flagship product conversion pages. Everyone, from designers to marketers to developers, is empowered to create a new experience. Plasmic also plugs into existing deployment and QA processes, so you can move fast with the guardrails you need. This increased velocity will help make Intuit even more agile in this dynamic market.

42203900.text: Best known for their financial solutions products, like TurboTax and QuickBooks, Intuit is a leader in building software and cloud solutions to power economic prosperity. This market leader chooses Plasmic to accelerate their go-to-market.

42203951.text: Want to build a page like this?
